pullRequests.title: feat(launcher): scaffold a desktop launcher for all four games
pullRequests.author: Veradictus
pullRequests.head: claude/pensive-wozniak-x52913
pullRequests.body:
A Tauri 2 desktop app in launcher/ that puts OpenRAC behind buttons for every version in games/ (rac1 PAL and NTSC-U, rac2, rac3, rac4): find your discs, place each build's inputs, set up, build, check, play in PCSX2, and open the level editor. It runs the checkout's own tools and streams their output; it hard-codes nothing a game.json already says.
This is scaffolding: the app, its look, the catalogue, the job runner and the repository-wide actions work; most per-game actions are written from…

commits.headline: docs(legal): rac1/pal is GPL v3 since 2026-10-07
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
rac1-decomp relicensed its own code to the GPL v3. LICENSE.md and open
question 1 now say so: code from rac1/pal or rac3 can only move into an
MIT directory with its authors' permission, MIT code can move the other
way, so the port tool's Lombyte-to-PAL direction stays open and PAL-to-
Lombyte needs agreement for code written after the move. The editor
keeps its MIT license (it moved here while rac1-decomp was MIT), and
rac2's functional port keeps its own MIT notice. The stale remark…

commits.headline: docs(workflow): build-fidelity rules, worker tiers, rac2 and rac3 changes
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
- rac1/pal: the build-fidelity rules (no step edits compiler output,
  options per whole file, enforced by --check), what counts as finished
  without C (remnant runs, joined functions), and the worker tiers
  measured on 2026-10-07 (tools first, a small-function swarm, Opus for
  near misses and long functions, Sonnet only with an answer key).
- rac2: shared native families, guarded batch finalisation, regions.
- rac3: three targets, `--target all`, `@ee29` and whole-file flags.
